 Ilia Topuria says UFC White House injury was inches away from ending career
 Ilia Topuria suffered serious injuries in his UFC White House defeat to Justin Gaethje in June, with the 29-year-old being left with a non-displaced fracture of both orbital bones and a broken nose
 Add to preferred sources Comments Tom Malley U.S. Sports Reporter 08:58 ET, 19 Nov 2026 View 3 Images Ilia Topuria suffered a brutal defeat to Justin Gaethje in the main event of UFC Freedom 250 in June
 Ilia Topuria has revealed just how close the injuries he sustained in his UFC White House defeat to Justin Gaethje came to ending his career, after being forced to forfeit at the end of the fourth round.
 ‌ 
 ‌ 
 Topuria, 29, suffered a brutal defeat - and the first of his professional MMA career - to Gaethje in the main event of UFC Freedom 250 in June, when he lost the UFC Lightweight Championship to the American as a result of a corner stoppage.
 Referee Marc Goddard brought proceedings to an end after Topuria's older brother and lead cornerman, Aleksandre Topuria, informed him that the previously undefeated fighter was done and could not continue due to serious injuries.
 ‌ 
 READ MORE : Justin Gaethje viciously fires back at Ilia Topuria's 'cheating' accusation READ MORE : Ilia Topuria changed Ferran Torres' life as relationship explained after Ibiza trip UFC CEO Dana White confirmed post-fight that Topuria was taken straight to hospital after being left "busted up" by Gaethje, where it was revealed the Spanish-Georgian star had been left with a non-displaced fracture of both orbital bones and a broken nose, leaving him struggling to see out of either eye.
 Surprisingly, Topuria did not require surgery for his injuries, with reports in his native Spain claiming at the time that his current plan was to simply rest and recover as he looks to eventually work his way back from his first career defeat.
 Five months after the brutal encounter with Gaethje, "El Matador" has now revealed just how close the damage he sustained came to ending his career, as he continues to await a return to full training.
 ‌ 
 View 3 Images Topuria was taken straight to hospital following his defeat to Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250
 "The problem would have been that I could never fight again," he told La Gazzetta Georgia . "When your orbital bones are fractured and you undergo surgery, they insert titanium plates. Once those plates are in place, you can never take another punch to that area."
 ‌ 
 Topuria also provided additional detail to Diario ABC , saying that if the tissue around his eye socket had moved by 0.5mm further, then the titanium plate would have had to be inserted, and he'd never have fought again.
 The good news for UFC fans is that Topuria has already made it clear he plans to return following his defeat, breaking his silence shortly after the UFC White House event with an Instagram post suggesting a rematch with Gaethje is on the cards.
 ‌ 
 "Justin, congratulations. You said you'd leave your mark on my face… and you did," Topuria wrote . "You took the sight from my right eye in the first round, and by the end of the second, from my left too."
 View 3 Images Topuria suffered a non-displaced fracture of both orbital bones as well as a broken nose from his fight with Gaethje
 He added: "I'll heal. I'll rest. And I'll return stronger, wiser, and far more dangerous. And trust me… this story between us is far from over. We will have our rematch."
 In September, Topuria confirmed that he had been officially cleared to compete again, posting on X : "Final medical tests done. I'm back. To all the clowns who've been talking s--- and counting me out this whole time, here I am.
 "Now let's see who's got the balls. Thanks to everyone for the support. Next time I'll make sure they check Justin's gloves so he doesn't put anything weird on them. See you soon."
